newsitem.title: USA: DSSI to sell control of company.
newsitem.headline: DSSI to sell control of company.

text.p: DSSI Corp said Tuesday it had agreed to sell control of the company to Michael Blumenfeld, who will buy 10 million shares of DSSI common for $2 million.
In addition, investors including current board members and their affiliates have agreed to buy 1.5 million DSSI shares for $300,000.
The deal is subject to shareholder approval.
Blumenfeld founded Sport Supply Group Inc and was chief executive and the largest shareholder of the Dallas-based company until December 1996.
DSSI said it will change its name ot Collegiate Pacific and will trade under a new symbol with the closing of the Blumenfeld deal.
It said Blumenfeld will designate a new DSSI board that will include one current director.

In a written statement, Blumenfeld said he expects rapid acceleration of DSSI's business in 1998 and expects annual growth rates of 50 percent for the "forseeable future," with strategic acquisitions, new licensing programs and corporate joint ventures expanding growth.
He said the operating focus of the company will be on a "very select group of high-margin, fast-moving products" that will allow it to maintain a small workforce and maximum profitability.
DSSI sold substantially all of its operating assets to Casco Standards Inc in June 1997.
